guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: extremely well documented — SRV's well-worn 1963/1962-hybrid Strat nicknamed "Number One" is among the most famous guitars in blues-rock.

tone.target: Texas blues Strat bite with singing sustain; cleanish amp edge
tone.profile: Texas blues Strat bite with singing sustain; cleanish amp edge
tone.summary: A classic Texas blues setup utilizing a Boost for mid-range punch, followed by a Silver Twin amp model to capture the bright, clean Fender sound, paired with a US 2x12 cabinet. A Spring reverb adds necessary vintage depth.
corrections: Keep it cleaner than gritty rock
No wah unless a specific part demands it

rig.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan & Double Trouble - Couldn’t Stand the Weather - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Simulate the Tube Screamer-style mid boost for lead lines and bite.
Provide a subtle, clean edge and grit without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to add harmonic richness and slight breakup, mimicking the natural compression of vintage Fender amps at high gain, rather than being a primary dirt source.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, clean Fender Vibroverb/Twin tone.
Provide the classic bright, articulate sound of a smaller Fender-style cabinet.
Slightly boost the mids and highs to enhance the 'Strat bite' and cut through the mix.
Optional subtle modulation for depth (kept off by default to avoid sounding too '80s').
blocks.gap: The Chorus is available but generally avoided in this specific blues context; it's included as a potential texture layer.

blocks.purpose: Add a touch of vintage depth and sustain, matching the 'light spring reverb' requirement.
Used for specific rhythmic fills or solos (optional).
blocks.gap: Not strictly necessary for the core tone, but included as a versatile option.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism with a more period-appropriate IR for vintage Fender tones.

proposals.reason: Improve the natural, open sound of a classic Fender cab.
